vred på.explanation: "Vred på" means "angry at". To name who you are angry at, put the person after "på" (at): "Jeg er vred på ham" (I am angry at him). When more than one person is angry, "vred" becomes "vrede": "Vi er vrede på chefen" (We are angry at the boss).

vrede.explanation: "Vrede" means "anger". To say someone feels anger: "Hun følte vrede, da han løj" (She felt anger when he lied). The same spelling is also the plural of "vred" (angry): "De er vrede" (They are angry).

vrøvl.explanation: "Vrøvl" means "nonsense". It is the noun for "at vrøvle" (to talk nonsense): "Hold op med at vrøvle!" (Stop talking nonsense!) It is blunt, so with someone you do not know well, say "Jeg er ikke enig" (I do not agree) instead.

våd.explanation: "Våd" means "wet". In front of a word that takes "et", add "t": "et vådt håndklæde" (a wet towel). With more than one thing, add "e": "våde hunde" (wet dogs).

vågen.explanation: "Vågen" means "awake". To ask if someone is awake: "Er du vågen?" (Are you awake?) Do not mix it up with "at vågne" (to wake up): "Jeg vågnede klokken syv" (I woke up at seven).

væk.explanation: "Væk" means "gone". To say you cannot find something: "Min nøgle er væk" (My key is gone). A different use: to say someone moves away, use "away": "Hun løber væk" (She runs away). "Gå væk!" (Go away!) is blunt.

vækst.explanation: "Vækst" means "growth". It is the noun for the verb "at vokse" (to grow): "Planterne vokser hurtigt" (The plants are growing fast). To talk about a country's economy: "økonomisk vækst" (economic growth).

vældig.explanation: "Vældig" means "very". To make a word stronger: "vældig glad" (very happy).

værd.explanation: "Værd" means "worth". To say how much something is worth, put "værd" after the amount: "Cyklen er tusind kroner værd" (The bike is worth a thousand kroner). To say something is worth doing, add "at" (to) before the verb: "værd at prøve" (worth trying).

værdifuld.explanation: "Værdifuld" means "valuable". It is built from "værdi" (value) and "fuld" (full). The same ending is in "smertefuld" (painful, literally "full of pain").

værdig.explanation: "Værdig" means "worthy". To name what the person deserves, add "til" (of): "værdig til respekt" (worthy of respect). A different meaning is "dignified": "et værdigt svar" (a dignified answer).

værdighed.explanation: "Værdighed" means "dignity". It is built from "værdig" (worthy). To say someone stays calm and proud: "Hun gik med værdighed" (She walked with dignity).

værdiløs.explanation: "Værdiløs" means "worthless". It is built from "værdi" (value) and "løs" (without). The ending "løs" is also in "hjælpeløs" (helpless) and "søvnløs" (sleepless).

værdsat.explanation: "Værdsat" means "appreciated". It comes from "at værdsætte" (to appreciate). To thank a coworker: "Du er en værdsat kollega" (You are an appreciated colleague).

værre.explanation: "Værre" means "worse". It is the form of "dårlig" (bad) for comparing two things: "Maden er værre her end hjemme" (The food is worse here than at home). To say a situation is quite bad: "et værre rod" (quite a mess).

værsgo.explanation: "Værsgo" means "here you go". To invite someone to do something, it means "go ahead". It is short for "vær så god" (be so good).

værst.explanation: "Værst" means "worst". It is the form of "dårlig" (bad) for the worst of all: "Det værste er, at vi mistede bussen" (The worst thing is that we missed the bus). For two things, use "værre" (worse): "Det er værre end i går" (It is worse than yesterday).

væsentlig.explanation: "Væsentlig" means "significant". To say it does not matter, put "ikke" (not) before it: "Det er ikke væsentligt, hvem der vinder" (It is not important who wins). For a person, say "vigtig" (important): "en vigtig person" (an important person).

en webshop.explanation: "En webshop" means "an online store". It is built from "web" (the internet) and "shop" (store). To say where you bought something: "Jeg har købt det i en webshop" (I bought it in an online store).

en webside.explanation: "En webside" means "a web page". It is built from "web" (the internet) and "side" (page). For a whole site, use "en hjemmeside" (a website): "Firmaets hjemmeside er ny" (The company's website is new).

en weekend.explanation: "En weekend" means "a weekend". To say on the weekend, use "i weekenden": "Vi ses i weekenden" (See you on the weekend). To wish someone well on a Friday: "God weekend!" (Have a good weekend!)

en weekendtur.explanation: "En weekendtur" means "a weekend trip". It is built from "weekend" (weekend) and "tur" (trip). The same "tur" is in "en biltur" (a car trip). To suggest one: "Skal vi tage på weekendtur?" (Shall we go on a weekend trip?)

en whisky.explanation: "En whisky" means "a whiskey". To offer a glass: "Vil du have en whisky?" (Would you like a whiskey?) To talk about the drink in general, leave out "en": "Jeg kan godt lide whisky" (I like whiskey).

en wrap.explanation: "En wrap" means "a wrap". To say what is inside: "en wrap med falafel" (a wrap with falafel).

et whiteboard.explanation: "Et whiteboard" means "a whiteboard". It is built from the English words "white" and "board". For a board you write on with chalk, use "en tavle" (a blackboard): "Læreren skriver med kridt på tavlen" (The teacher writes with chalk on the board).
